newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi says not deaf to pleas for tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi says not deaf to pleas for tax cuts.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Friday he was not insensitive to calls from the business sector for a reduction in taxes but Italy could not afford that until public accounts had been cleaned-up.
"I am not deaf to the warnings over fiscal pressure," Prodi told a conference staged by the national association of artisans and craftsmen.
"But the government has to (reduce tax) in the same way as in other modern countries...that is after inflation has been reduced and the economy relaunched," he added.

Italy's centre-left government has upped the fiscal pressure over the past year as it tries to prepare state accounts for the launch of the planned single European currency. Italy's tax rates are among the highest in the European Union.
Italian business leaders have warned that unless taxes are cut steady economic growth will prove impossible.
But Prodi said Italy could only cut taxes in line with a corresponding fall in the country's huge debt servicing costs.

The prime minister said the fall in the spread between Italian and German 10-year bonds, which stood at around 400 basis points just before Prodi took office in May 1996 and are now under 100 basis points, would save the Treasury around 60 trillion lire ($35 billion) in lower interest charges.
"We have made an extraordinary step forward and the financial markets believe in this process," Prodi said. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
